3. Research questions & sub-products. # Research questions & sub-products. 1. Translating research objectives into research questions. 2. Translating research objectives into sub-products. From objectives to research questions**. Formulating research questions helps in getting an overview of the information that needs to be collected. The *knowledge objective* is often easy to transform into a research question. If the knowledge objective of a study is to gain insight into the experience of care received on ward X, this can be translated into the research question: ‘How is the care received on ward X experienced?’. If the design objective of a research project is to develop an app that allows clients to keep a diary, then relevant questions are, for example: ‘What are the functional requirements for the app?’ or ‘Which parameters should the app development be subject to?’. By going through all the formulated objectives within a research design, a set of main- and sub-questions can be created. Research questions are an important guiding element in a research project. A well-formulated research question is a prerequisite for good research. A well-formulated research question is:. A good research question immediately makes clear which research function the question refers to (for an explanation of these functions, refer to the knowledge clip above). Andriessen (2011) provides an overview with example questions for each of Oost & Markenhof’s (2002) six research functions:. ## Examples of research questions for each research function. Overview with examples of research questions for each of the six research functions of Oost & Markenhof (2002). Formulating and organising sub-products is helpful in structuring the research project and developing an approach. Sub-products make explicit which concrete intermediate products are needed to achieve the objectives of the research project. Making sub-products explicit is appropriate in research projects in which the design objective, professionalisation objective and/or change objective are important, as it can be used to indicate the manner in which the objectives will be realised. Because the realisation of a specific sub-product often requires new knowledge in turn, making sub-products explicit often also leads to new sub-questions for the research project. The sub-questions and sub-products formulated serve as the basis for developing the research approach.

results.content: In order to conduct a successful research study, it is essential to have a clear understanding of the research objectives and the methods that will be used to achieve them. One of the key components of a research proposal is the research question. A research question is a concise and focused statement that identifies the main objective of the study and guides the research process. It serves as the foundation for the entire research proposal and helps to define the scope and direction of the study. Formulating precise research questions in a proposal is crucial as they directly align with the study's objectives, shaping the direction and focus of the entire research process. We will discuss what research questions are, why they are important, provide examples of research questions, and offer guidance on how to formulate effective research questions for a research proposal. ## What is a Research Question in a Research Proposal? # How to Formulate Effective Research Questions. Formulating effective research questions is one of the most critical steps in the research process. A well-defined research question provides the foundation for a solid investigation, guiding every step from data collection to analysis. This article provides a step-by-step approach to help you formulate research questions that will lead to meaningful and impactful research. The first step in formulating a research question is to identify a broad area of interest. These notes will guide you as you refine your topic and formulate your research question. For example, you might narrow down the broad topic of “AI in healthcare” to something more specific, like “The effectiveness of AI algorithms in diagnosing cardiovascular diseases.” This refined focus will lead to a research question that is more specific and manageable. Now that you have a more focused topic, it's time to formulate your actual research question. The question should be clear, concise, and specific enough that it can be answered through empirical research. At this stage, you should also ensure that the question is measurable and researchable using available methods, data, and tools. results.title: How to use sub-questions to strengthen research questions
results.content: # The Role of Sub-Questions in Strengthening Main Research Questions. Research projects often begin with a broad main question that guides the entire investigation. Sub-questions address this challenge by breaking the main question into smaller, manageable components. By focusing on specific aspects of the main question, sub-questions ensure clarity, depth, and methodological precision. This report explores how sub-questions strengthen primary research questions, providing practical strategies and examples to illustrate their utility. ## Understanding Main Research Questions and Sub-Questions. ### Defining the Main Research Question. A main research question represents the core objective of a study. For instance, a main question might ask, *"How can communication between employees and managers be improved within Organization X?"*. 1. **Simplifying Complexity**: By isolating specific aspects of the main question, sub-questions make the research process manageable. ### Aligning Sub-Questions with the Main Question. Sub-questions must directly contribute to answering the main question. For example, a sub-question asking, *"What are the effects of social media on mental health?"* is overly vague.
